prompt: Thanks, but I was interested in the Manhattan distance. How can I compute it?
reply: The Manhattan distance, also known as the L1 distance, is a measure of the absolute differences between two points in a grid-based space, such as a city grid. To calculate the Manhattan distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2), you simply add the absolute differences of their coordinates: d = |x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2| In a 3-dimensional space, you would extend the formula to: d = |x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2| + |z1 - z2|
